content: Whenever in this chapter a petition, order, resolution, complaint, or other document  refers to a principal act, the name, if any, of the principal act, with its citation  shall be set forth in such document.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58004
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58004
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

(a) “District” means a tax or assessment district.

(b) “Governing body” means the board of directors of a district or equivalent board  or body.

(c) “ Principal act ” means the law providing for the creation of a particular district or type of district.

(d) “ Supervising authority ” means the board of supervisors of the county in which is situated all or most of  the land in a district, or body authorized by law to initiate or hear proceedings  for the creation of a district.

(e) “ Project ” means the work, improvement, or acquisition, or any combination thereof undertaken  by a district.

(f) “ Owner ” includes joint owner, co-owner, guardian, executor, administrator, or other person  holding property in trust under court appointment.

(g) “Requisite number of petitioners” means the number of qualified petitioners prescribed  by the principal act.

(h) “Requisite number of protestants” means the number of qualified protestants prescribed  by the principal act.

(i) “ Clerk ” means the clerk of the supervising authority.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58008
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58008
content: Proof of publication may be by affidavit of the owner, publisher, printer, or clerk  of the newspaper. The affidavit is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in it.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58009
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58009
content: If a district is situated in a county in which no newspaper of general circulation  is published, the notice shall be posted in three public places in the district for  the same period as if published.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58007
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58007
content: Unless otherwise expressly provided, each notice shall be published once a week for  three successive weeks prior to the date set for the event of which notice is given.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58011
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58011
content: In case of a conflict between the provisions of this chapter and the provisions of  the law providing for the creation of a particular district or type of district, the  provisions of this chapter shall prevail.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58010
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58010
content: Proof of posting may be by affidavit of the person posting the notice. The affidavit is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in it.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58030
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58030
content: When the principal act authorizes or requires a petition, formation proceedings shall  be commenced by petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58031
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58031
content: The petition shall be signed by the requisite number of petitioners and addressed  to and filed with the supervising authority.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58032
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58032
content: The petition may be filed in sections. Each section shall comply with all the requirements for a petition, except that  it need not contain all the signatures required for the petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58034
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58034
content:
The petition shall:

(a) State the proposed name for the district.

(b) Set forth the district boundaries or describe the land situated in the district.

(c) Request that the district be formed pursuant to the principal act.

(d) Describe generally the nature of the proposed project and, based upon the functions  proposed to be performed by the district, an estimate verified by the proponents of  the first year's estimated income and expenses and estimated expenditures for capital  improvements.

(e) Comply with any additional requirements of the principal act.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing›CA GOVT § 58060
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 3. Preliminary Hearing › CA GOVT § 58060
content: Upon presentation and filing of the formation petition the supervising authority shall  fix a time and place for its hearing. The hearing shall not be less than 20 nor more than 40 days after presentation and  filing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58033
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58033
content: Before publication of the petition, a petitioner may withdraw his signature by filing  with the clerk a signed statement of his intention to withdraw his signature from  the petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing›CA GOVT § 58061
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 3. Preliminary Hearing › CA GOVT § 58061
content: If the principal act or any other law applicable to the formation of the district  requires the making of an investigation of and a report on the project, the hearing  may be continued from time to time to enable the making of such investigation and  report. Such continuance shall not exceed three months.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58090
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58090
content: The supervising authority shall fix the time and place for the final hearing on the  petition and shall order the clerk to give notice of the hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58091
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58091
content:
The notice of final hearing shall state:

(a) The name and nature of the district.

(b) That the petition may be inspected at the clerk's office.

(c) The boundaries of the proposed district and the estimated initial annual special  ad valorem tax rate to the taxable property within the proposed district as computed  based on the verified information provided pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 58034 of this code.

(d) The time and place for the final hearing.

(e) That protests will be considered at the hearing.

(f) That written requests for exclusion from or inclusion of land in the proposed  district will be heard and considered.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58092
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58092
content: The clerk shall give notice of the final hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58094
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58094
content: If the notice is materially defective, the supervising authority shall reset the hearing  and cause new notice to be given.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58093
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58093
content: The supervising authority is not deprived of jurisdiction to proceed with the hearing,  and no action on the petition is invalid, because of clerical error in the notice.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58095
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58095
content: If the supervising authority determines that the petition does not comply with the  law, the matter may be dismissed without prejudice to the right to present a new petition  on the same matter.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58096
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58096
content: A finding by the supervising authority in favor of the genuineness and sufficiency  of the petition and notice is conclusive against all persons except the State in a  proceeding brought by the Attorney General within one year after the order establishing  and describing the boundaries of the district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58097
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58097
content: Oral or written protest may be made at the hearing by any person interested in the  formation of the proposed district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58098
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58098
content: Any protest to the regularity or sufficiency of the proceedings shall be written and  shall clearly set forth the defects to which objection is made.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58099
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58099
content: Written protests shall be filed with the clerk on or before the time fixed for the  final hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58101
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58101
content: At the hearing any owner of land in the proposed district may present to the supervising  authority a written request for exclusion of all or part of such land.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58100
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58100
content: The hearing may be continued from time to time not exceeding 60 days.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58103
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58103
content: If the supervising authority finds that protest has been made, prior to the supervising  authority's final determination for formation, by the owners of real property within  the proposed district the assessed value of which, as shown by the last equalized  assessment roll, constitutes more than one-half of the total assessed value of the  real property within the proposed district, the proceeding shall terminate. The supervising authority shall order the proceedings terminated when such protests  are received.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58104
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58104
content: The supervising authority shall not consider a petition or other proceedings for the  formation of the same district for the same project until after one year from the  order of termination.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58102
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58102
content: At the hearing any owner of land outside the proposed district may present to the  supervising authority a written request for inclusion of such land.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58105
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58105
content: If at the final hearing the supervising authority determines that the project is feasible,  economically sound, and for the public interest, it shall fix the boundaries of the  proposed district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58105.1
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58105.1
content: If at the final hearing the supervising authority determines that the project, or  the proposed district as its boundaries are described in the petition or as changed  by the supervising authority as hereafter provided, is infeasible, not economically  sound, or not for the public interest, it may terminate the proceedings.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58107
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58107
content: The supervising authority may make such inclusion upon the owner's application or  upon giving him notice of and hearing on the inclusion.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58108
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58108
content: The clerk shall publish notice of inclusion and mail it, postage prepaid, to the address  of the owner of such land as shown by the last equalized county assessment roll and  to any person who has filed with the clerk his name, address, and a description of  land in which he has a legal or equitable interest.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58106
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58106
content:
At the final hearing the supervising authority shall exclude any land which it finds  will not be benefited by the proposed project and shall make a specific finding as  to each parcel of land with respect to which a written request for exclusion has been  presented on the question of whether it will or will not be benefited by the proposed  project. In making such finding the supervising authority shall consider present use of such  land, reasonable prospective use, topography, the nature of the proposed improvements,  and any other pertinent factors. The present use of lands for rights-of-way for railroads, power and communication  lines, or other public utility facilities shall be presumed by the supervising authority  to be permanent.

The supervising authority may include any land if it finds that the land will be benefited  and that its inclusion will be to the interest of the district.

If lands are excluded by the supervising authority pursuant to this section, such  lands shall not thereafter be annexed to or included in the district in the absence  of a finding, based on substantial evidence, of a change in the circumstances upon  which the decision to exclude such lands was based.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58109
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58109
content: The notice shall describe the land proposed to be included and state the time and  place at which objections to inclusion will be heard.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58110
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58110
content: If the supervising authority determines that the district should be established, by  resolution it shall fix and describe the boundaries, and designate a name for, the  district. The name may be that proposed in the petition or any other name the supervising  authority selects.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58000
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58000
content: This chapter may be cited as the District Organization Law.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58001
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58001
content: It is the purpose of this chapter to make available a procedure for the organization,  operation and government of districts.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58002
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58002
content: This chapter applies only when and to the extent that it is adopted or incorporated  by reference in a law providing for a particular district or type of district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58130
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58130
content: Within 20 days after the adoption of the resolution establishing the boundaries, the  supervising authority shall call and give notice of an election to be held in the  proposed district to determine whether the district shall be formed and to select  the elective officers, if any, of the district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58004
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58004
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

(a) “District” means a tax or assessment district.

(b) “Governing body” means the board of directors of a district or equivalent board  or body.

(c) “ Principal act ” means the law providing for the creation of a particular district or type of district.

(d) “ Supervising authority ” means the board of supervisors of the county in which is situated all or most of  the land in a district, or body authorized by law to initiate or hear proceedings  for the creation of a district.

(e) “ Project ” means the work, improvement, or acquisition, or any combination thereof undertaken  by a district.

(f) “ Owner ” includes joint owner, co-owner, guardian, executor, administrator, or other person  holding property in trust under court appointment.

(g) “Requisite number of petitioners” means the number of qualified petitioners prescribed  by the principal act.

(h) “Requisite number of protestants” means the number of qualified protestants prescribed  by the principal act.

(i) “ Clerk ” means the clerk of the supervising authority.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58005
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58005
content: Whenever in this chapter a petition, order, resolution, complaint, or other document  refers to a principal act, the name, if any, of the principal act, with its citation  shall be set forth in such document.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58006
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58006
content: When this chapter or the principal act requires publication of a notice, publication  shall be in a newspaper of general circulation published and circulated within the  district, or if there is none, in the newspaper of general circulation published nearest  to the district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58007
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58007
content: Unless otherwise expressly provided, each notice shall be published once a week for  three successive weeks prior to the date set for the event of which notice is given.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58132
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58132
content: If a majority of the votes cast at the election favors the organization of the district,  by resolution entered on its minutes the supervising authority shall declare the district  duly organized under the principal act, give the designated name of the district,  and describe its boundaries.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58008
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58008
content: Proof of publication may be by affidavit of the owner, publisher, printer, or clerk  of the newspaper. The affidavit is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in it.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58010
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58010
content: Proof of posting may be by affidavit of the person posting the notice. The affidavit is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in it.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58009
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58009
content: If a district is situated in a county in which no newspaper of general circulation  is published, the notice shall be posted in three public places in the district for  the same period as if published.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58011
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58011
content: In case of a conflict between the provisions of this chapter and the provisions of  the law providing for the creation of a particular district or type of district, the  provisions of this chapter shall prevail.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58030
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58030
content: When the principal act authorizes or requires a petition, formation proceedings shall  be commenced by petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58032
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58032
content: The petition may be filed in sections. Each section shall comply with all the requirements for a petition, except that  it need not contain all the signatures required for the petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58031
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58031
content: The petition shall be signed by the requisite number of petitioners and addressed  to and filed with the supervising authority.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58133
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58133
content: Immediately after the passing of the resolution declaring the organization of the  district, the clerk shall file a certified copy of the resolution with the Secretary  of State and for record in the office of the county recorder of each county in which  any land in the district is situated. Upon such filing the organization of the district is complete.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58033
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58033
content: Before publication of the petition, a petitioner may withdraw his signature by filing  with the clerk a signed statement of his intention to withdraw his signature from  the petition.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing›CA GOVT § 58060
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 3. Preliminary Hearing › CA GOVT § 58060
content: Upon presentation and filing of the formation petition the supervising authority shall  fix a time and place for its hearing. The hearing shall not be less than 20 nor more than 40 days after presentation and  filing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58034
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 2. Petition for Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 2. Petition for Formation › CA GOVT § 58034
content:
The petition shall:

(a) State the proposed name for the district.

(b) Set forth the district boundaries or describe the land situated in the district.

(c) Request that the district be formed pursuant to the principal act.

(d) Describe generally the nature of the proposed project and, based upon the functions  proposed to be performed by the district, an estimate verified by the proponents of  the first year's estimated income and expenses and estimated expenditures for capital  improvements.

(e) Comply with any additional requirements of the principal act.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58131
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58131
content:
The election shall be called and conducted, and any candidates shall be nominated  as in general district elections except:

(a) The supervising authority shall establish election precincts, designate the polling  places, publish notice, and appoint the election board.

(b) The election returns shall be forwarded to the supervising authority which shall  canvass them and declare the election results at its next regular meeting following  the election.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing›CA GOVT § 58061
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 3. Preliminary Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 3. Preliminary Hearing › CA GOVT § 58061
content: If the principal act or any other law applicable to the formation of the district  requires the making of an investigation of and a report on the project, the hearing  may be continued from time to time to enable the making of such investigation and  report. Such continuance shall not exceed three months.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58092
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58092
content: The clerk shall give notice of the final hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58091
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58091
content:
The notice of final hearing shall state:

(a) The name and nature of the district.

(b) That the petition may be inspected at the clerk's office.

(c) The boundaries of the proposed district and the estimated initial annual special  ad valorem tax rate to the taxable property within the proposed district as computed  based on the verified information provided pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 58034 of this code.

(d) The time and place for the final hearing.

(e) That protests will be considered at the hearing.

(f) That written requests for exclusion from or inclusion of land in the proposed  district will be heard and considered.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58090
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58090
content: The supervising authority shall fix the time and place for the final hearing on the  petition and shall order the clerk to give notice of the hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58093
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58093
content: The supervising authority is not deprived of jurisdiction to proceed with the hearing,  and no action on the petition is invalid, because of clerical error in the notice.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58095
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58095
content: If the supervising authority determines that the petition does not comply with the  law, the matter may be dismissed without prejudice to the right to present a new petition  on the same matter.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58094
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58094
content: If the notice is materially defective, the supervising authority shall reset the hearing  and cause new notice to be given.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 7. Validating Proceedings›CA GOVT § 58200
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 1. The District Organization Law›Article 7. Validating Proceedings
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 1. The District Organization Law › Article 7. Validating Proceedings › CA GOVT § 58200
content: An action to determine the legality of the existence of the district may be brought  pursuant to Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 860 ) of Title 10 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58097
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58097
content: Oral or written protest may be made at the hearing by any person interested in the  formation of the proposed district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58099
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58099
content: Written protests shall be filed with the clerk on or before the time fixed for the  final hearing.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58096
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58096
content: A finding by the supervising authority in favor of the genuineness and sufficiency  of the petition and notice is conclusive against all persons except the State in a  proceeding brought by the Attorney General within one year after the order establishing  and describing the boundaries of the district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58098
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58098
content: Any protest to the regularity or sufficiency of the proceedings shall be written and  shall clearly set forth the defects to which objection is made.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58101
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58101
content: At the hearing any owner of land in the proposed district may present to the supervising  authority a written request for exclusion of all or part of such land.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58100
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58100
content: The hearing may be continued from time to time not exceeding 60 days.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58102
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58102
content: At the hearing any owner of land outside the proposed district may present to the  supervising authority a written request for inclusion of such land.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58103
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58103
content: If the supervising authority finds that protest has been made, prior to the supervising  authority's final determination for formation, by the owners of real property within  the proposed district the assessed value of which, as shown by the last equalized  assessment roll, constitutes more than one-half of the total assessed value of the  real property within the proposed district, the proceeding shall terminate. The supervising authority shall order the proceedings terminated when such protests  are received.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58105.1
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58105.1
content: If at the final hearing the supervising authority determines that the project, or  the proposed district as its boundaries are described in the petition or as changed  by the supervising authority as hereafter provided, is infeasible, not economically  sound, or not for the public interest, it may terminate the proceedings.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58104
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58104
content: The supervising authority shall not consider a petition or other proceedings for the  formation of the same district for the same project until after one year from the  order of termination.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58105
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58105
content: If at the final hearing the supervising authority determines that the project is feasible,  economically sound, and for the public interest, it shall fix the boundaries of the  proposed district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58106
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58106
content:
At the final hearing the supervising authority shall exclude any land which it finds  will not be benefited by the proposed project and shall make a specific finding as  to each parcel of land with respect to which a written request for exclusion has been  presented on the question of whether it will or will not be benefited by the proposed  project. In making such finding the supervising authority shall consider present use of such  land, reasonable prospective use, topography, the nature of the proposed improvements,  and any other pertinent factors. The present use of lands for rights-of-way for railroads, power and communication  lines, or other public utility facilities shall be presumed by the supervising authority  to be permanent.

The supervising authority may include any land if it finds that the land will be benefited  and that its inclusion will be to the interest of the district.

If lands are excluded by the supervising authority pursuant to this section, such  lands shall not thereafter be annexed to or included in the district in the absence  of a finding, based on substantial evidence, of a change in the circumstances upon  which the decision to exclude such lands was based.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58109
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58109
content: The notice shall describe the land proposed to be included and state the time and  place at which objections to inclusion will be heard.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58108
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58108
content: The clerk shall publish notice of inclusion and mail it, postage prepaid, to the address  of the owner of such land as shown by the last equalized county assessment roll and  to any person who has filed with the clerk his name, address, and a description of  land in which he has a legal or equitable interest.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58107
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58107
content: The supervising authority may make such inclusion upon the owner's application or  upon giving him notice of and hearing on the inclusion.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58130
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58130
content: Within 20 days after the adoption of the resolution establishing the boundaries, the  supervising authority shall call and give notice of an election to be held in the  proposed district to determine whether the district shall be formed and to select  the elective officers, if any, of the district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58133
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58133
content: Immediately after the passing of the resolution declaring the organization of the  district, the clerk shall file a certified copy of the resolution with the Secretary  of State and for record in the office of the county recorder of each county in which  any land in the district is situated. Upon such filing the organization of the district is complete.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58131
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58131
content:
The election shall be called and conducted, and any candidates shall be nominated  as in general district elections except:

(a) The supervising authority shall establish election precincts, designate the polling  places, publish notice, and appoint the election board.

(b) The election returns shall be forwarded to the supervising authority which shall  canvass them and declare the election results at its next regular meeting following  the election.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing›CA GOVT § 58110
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 4. Final Hearing
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 4. Final Hearing › CA GOVT § 58110
content: If the supervising authority determines that the district should be established, by  resolution it shall fix and describe the boundaries, and designate a name for, the  district. The name may be that proposed in the petition or any other name the supervising  authority selects.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 7. Validating Proceedings›CA GOVT § 58200
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 7. Validating Proceedings
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 7. Validating Proceedings › CA GOVT § 58200
content: An action to determine the legality of the existence of the district may be brought  pursuant to Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 860 ) of Title 10 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation›CA GOVT § 58132
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Article 5. Formation
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Article 5. Formation › CA GOVT § 58132
content: If a majority of the votes cast at the election favors the organization of the district,  by resolution entered on its minutes the supervising authority shall declare the district  duly organized under the principal act, give the designated name of the district,  and describe its boundaries.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58850
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58850
content:
Unless the provisions or context otherwise require, the following definitions shall  govern the construction of this chapter:

(a) “ County surveyor ” means the county surveyor or such other county officer or employee as the board  of supervisors may designate.

(b) “ Proposal ” means any proposal for the formation of a new, or a change in the boundaries of  an existing, district exercising functions that are, or may be, supported by taxes  or special assessment taxes levied on property within the district and collected with  county taxes. This chapter does not apply to proposals concerning special assessment districts  formed for the purpose of providing various municipal and county improvements, or  to a municipal utility district, or a transit district organized under the Transit  District Law (Division 10, commencing with Section 24501, of the Public Utilities Code ), whose boundaries include all or portions of two or more counties.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58854
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58854
content: Within 30 days after filing, the county surveyor shall review and report on boundaries  set forth in the proposal. Failure to report on a proposal within said 30-day period shall be deemed approval  of the boundaries as set forth therein.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58856
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58856
content:
Factors to be considered by the county surveyor in review of a proposal shall include:

(a) The definiteness and certainty of the proposed boundaries;

(b) Conformance of the proposed boundaries with lines of ownership, as shown on the  last equalized assessment roll of the county or by documents of record in the office  of the county recorder; and

(c) Other similar matters of public interest resulting from the location of the proposed  boundaries.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58855
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58855
content:
Within 10 days after the filing of any proposal, the county surveyor shall give written  notice as provided in Section 58855.5 by mailing notice of such filing:

(a) To each city, county, or district the boundaries of which contain all or any portion  of the lands described in the proposal; and

(b) To each person who has filed a written request for special notice of such filings  of such proposals with the county surveyor.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58855.5
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58855.5

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58852
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58852
content: Prior to circulation of a petition, if such circulation is required, or otherwise  prior to filing with the board of supervisors or with the governing body of a district,  the proposal shall be submitted to the county surveyor as provided in this chapter. Each such proposal shall be accompanied by a map showing the boundaries of the territory  involved and by a specific detailed legal description of the boundaries of such territory.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58853
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58853
content: If the territory involved in the proposal is located in two or more counties, a copy  of the proposal shall be filed with the county surveyor of each such county. The county surveyor of each such county shall have jurisdiction over and shall report  upon those portions of the boundaries and territory which shall be located within  each such county.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts›CA GOVT § 58901
path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58901
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

(a) “ Proposal ” means any proposal for the formation of a new, or change in the boundaries of an  existing, district.

(b) “ Supervising authority ” means the board of supervisors, city council or the governing body authorized by  law to act upon proceedings for the formation of a new, or change in boundaries of  an existing, district.

(c) “District” means any tax, assessment or any other district except as otherwise  provided in Section 58902 .

(d) “ Clerk ” means the clerk or secretary of the supervising authority.

(e) “ Principal act ” means the law providing for the creation or change in boundaries of a district.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58851
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58851
content: The county surveyor and the county assessor shall review the boundary description  contained in those proposals which are not subject to the jurisdiction of the local  agency formation commission pursuant to Chapter 6.6 (commencing with Section 54775 ) of Part 1 of Division 2 of Title 5 or Division 1 (commencing with Section 56000 ), Title 6 of this code. Whenever the county boundary commission is referred to in state law, the reference  shall be deemed to be to the local agency formation commission when the reference  is in connection with any proposal over which the local agency formation commission  has jurisdiction.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58857
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58857
content: If he deems it to be in the public interest, the county surveyor may hold a public  hearing on the proposal. Notice of any such hearing shall be given to the same cities and districts as were  given notice pursuant to Section 58855 and may be given to such other cities, districts, public agencies, or persons as  the county surveyor may direct.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58858
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58858
content:
The county surveyor may make changes in the boundaries set forth in a proposal if:

(a) The proponents consent; and

(b) The territory contained within the revised boundaries complies with the requirements  of any applicable law and does not include any territory which could not have been  included at the time of the filing of the proposal.

If written notice was previously given pursuant to Section 58855 , within five days after making any such change, the county surveyor shall give written  notice thereof to any city or district, within three miles of the changed boundaries,  which was not previously given notice.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58861
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58861
content: Before acting upon any proposal, the legislative body having jurisdiction shall consider  the report of the county surveyor and give it such weight as in its judgment the public  interest requires.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58859
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58859
content: The county surveyor shall deliver a copy of his report together with any recommendations  made by the county assessor to the proponents and to the legislative body having jurisdiction  to conduct appropriate proceedings.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries›CA GOVT § 58860
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3. Change of Boundaries › CA GOVT § 58860
content: If the proponents do not accept the county surveyor's recommendations as contained  in his report, they shall file a statement of reasons with the legislative body having  jurisdiction to conduct the appropriate proceedings. The proponents shall also furnish a copy of such statement to the county surveyor. The proposal may be circulated or filed with the board of supervisors or the governing  body of the district, if any, only after such a report has been furnished.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts›CA GOVT § 58900
path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58900
content: It is the purpose of this chapter to require that notice of a proposal be given to  all owners of the real property described therein prior to the time the proposal is  acted upon by the supervising authority.

content: Except as herein otherwise provided, this chapter shall apply to all districts. This chapter shall not apply to any boundary change which is approved by all of  the owners of real property proposed to be included within, or proposed to be excluded  from, the district, nor to any proceeding commenced or conducted with respect to forming  a metropolitan water district or separation of grade district or changing the boundaries  thereof.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58004
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58004
content:
As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires:

(a) “District” means a tax or assessment district.

(b) “Governing body” means the board of directors of a district or equivalent board  or body.

(c) “ Principal act ” means the law providing for the creation of a particular district or type of district.

(d) “ Supervising authority ” means the board of supervisors of the county in which is situated all or most of  the land in a district, or body authorized by law to initiate or hear proceedings  for the creation of a district.

(e) “ Project ” means the work, improvement, or acquisition, or any combination thereof undertaken  by a district.

(f) “ Owner ” includes joint owner, co-owner, guardian, executor, administrator, or other person  holding property in trust under court appointment.

(g) “Requisite number of petitioners” means the number of qualified petitioners prescribed  by the principal act.

(h) “Requisite number of protestants” means the number of qualified protestants prescribed  by the principal act.

(i) “ Clerk ” means the clerk of the supervising authority.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts›CA GOVT § 58904
path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58904
content:
The notice of filing or other submission of the proposal shall contain the matters  specified by the law under which the proposal is made. In lieu thereof it shall be sufficient if the notice of filing or other submission  of the proposal shall contain the following:

(a) The nature of the proposal.

(b) A general description or map of the territory included in the proposal.

(c) The time and place of the first public hearing on the proposal if a public hearing  is required by other provisions of law to be held upon the proposal, or the time and  place upon which the supervising authority will take initial action upon the proposal.

title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58007

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58008
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58008
content: Proof of publication may be by affidavit of the owner, publisher, printer, or clerk  of the newspaper. The affidavit is prima facie evidence of the facts stated in it.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General›CA GOVT § 58009
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 1. General
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Article 1. General › CA GOVT § 58009
content: If a district is situated in a county in which no newspaper of general circulation  is published, the notice shall be posted in three public places in the district for  the same period as if published.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts›CA GOVT § 58905
path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58905
content: Every owner of real property, including property assessed by the State under Section 14, Article XIII of the Constitution , is hereby authorized to file a statement each fiscal year with the county assessor,  showing his name, address, and a description of the property owned by him, together  with a request that a notice of all proposals affecting such property shall be mailed  to him at such address. The statement and request shall be effective only for the fiscal year in which it  was filed. The fee for filing a statement and request is one dollar and fifty cents ($1.50). The property owner shall furnish a copy of the statement and request to the clerk  of any supervising authority having a request for same on file with the county assessor,  and this chapter shall be ineffective with respect to the actions of that supervising  authority unless its clerk shall have received a copy of the statement and request.

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Article 2. Petition for Formation›CA GOVT § 58030

path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts›CA GOVT § 58906
path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58906
content: If the principal act requires notice to be mailed by first-class mail to all owners  of property described in the proposal, including the owners of state assessed property,  notice shall be mailed in the form and manner, and at the time, required by such act. If the principal act does not require such notice, the clerk shall cause a notice  of the filing or other submission of the proposal to be mailed by post card or first  class mail, postage prepaid, to every owner of real property described in the proposal  who has filed the statement authorized by the preceding section, at the address shown  on such statement, at least 10 days prior to the first hearing or initial action on  the proposal. The clerk of the supervising authority may, upon completion of the mailing of such  notices, file an affidavit with the supervising authority stating that notices have  been mailed to all property owners entitled thereto under the provisions of this chapter. The affidavit of the clerk shall be conclusive evidence as to the mailing or nonmailing  of any notice. Mailing of notice to all property owners who have filed a request therefor with  the county assessor, as authorized by Section 58905 , shall be deemed sufficient compliance with this chapter for all purposes.

path_nodes: Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
parent_path: CALIFORNIA›Title 6. Districts›Division 1. General›Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts
title: CALIFORNIA Statutes › CALIFORNIA › Title 6. Districts › Division 1. General › Chapter 3.5. Notice of Formation or Change in Boundaries of Districts › CA GOVT § 58907
content: No proceeding shall be held invalid for omission of the clerk of the supervising body  to mail the notice required by this chapter to any property owner unless such owner  objects to such omission within 30 days after the public hearing or initial action  with reference to which such notice was omitted. No objection shall be considered unless it is made in writing, signed, under oath  by such owner or his duly authorized representative, and filed with the clerk of the  supervising authority. Upon the expiration of said 30 days, the clerk may file an affidavit stating whether  or not any property owner entitled to a mailed notice under this chapter who has not  been mailed such notice, has filed the objection herein authorized. The affidavit of the clerk shall be conclusive evidence as to the filing or nonfiling  of objections within the period of 30 days as above required. If a valid objection is filed within the time allowed, the supervising authority  shall conduct another hearing or reconsider its initial action on the proposal, after  complying with the notice provisions of this chapter and the principal act under which  the proposal was initiated. The time allowed by such principal act for the taking of any proceedings subsequent  to the initial action or hearing shall be extended for such additional time as may  be required to comply with this chapter.
